title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - Academy of Art University, School of Art Education - Teacher Internship and Practica Program - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement by and between the District and Academy of Art University, School of Art Education (University or AAU), a California private university, for the latter to provide an Intern Partnership Program and Practica Program, applying to Teaching Credentials, Service Credentials, and Certificates, with respect to the following categories: K-12 Education-Single Subject and Designated Subject, Art Education, including Bilingual Education, Added or Supplementary Authorizations, and Early Completion Option (ECO; and for Pre-Credential Graduate Support Programs at the University (credentials and certifications specified herein referred to as Covered Programs, Program Categories, or Covered Categories …), via the Talent/Human Resources Department, for the term July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025, at no cost to the District.
headline: Partners with Academy of Art University on teacher internships at no cost, through June 2025
summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) sets up an intern partnership and practica (supervised hands-on training) program with Academy of Art University's School of Art Education. It runs July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025 at no cost to the district, and the term began before this approval.
vendor_name: Academy of Art University, School of Art Education
pulled_from_consent: Taken off the consent vote, then approved on a later consent report on April 12.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2022-2023 - Bela Bhasin - English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2022-2023 by and between the District and Bela Bhasin, Oakland, CA, for the latter to create tools to identify 1) Culturally responsive strategies currently being used at school for improving connectedness, especially for ELL and AA students, (i.e., Teacher Focus Group Guide & Leadership Interview Guide); 2) Conduct a series of family focus groups to gather baseline data on connectedness and belonging with a focus on families of ELL and AA students; 3) Conduct a series of teacher focus groups and leadership interviews to identify culturally responsive strategies for improving connectedness for ELL and AA students and families; 4) Support site leaders to make sense of the data gathered and identify the next steps and provide thought partnership as needed, via English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department, for the period of January 16, 2023 through June 30, 2023, in an amount not to exceed $15,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $15,000 for a consultant to study school connectedness for English learner and Black families
summary: A consultant will build tools and run family and teacher focus groups and leadership interviews on how connected students and families feel to school, focusing on English language learner (ELL) and African American (AA) students and families. The consultant will also help school leaders understand the data and plan next steps. The agreement runs January 16, 2023 through June 30, 2023, up to $15,000, and the board is ratifying (approving after the fact) an agreement whose service period has already begun.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

summary: A consultant will facilitate monthly meetings with district teachers on supporting English language learners with interrupted formal education (students who have missed significant schooling) in math classrooms. The combined $7,810.91 is carried over to fiscal year 2023-24. This reallocates money already in the school's 2022-23 plan.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Measure N Commission - March 7, 2023 - Louise Waters, Chairperson
title: Measure N Commission - 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/ Budget Modification – McClymonds High School
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of the Measure N Commission, of a 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/Budget modification for McClymonds High School reducing from three different strategic actions; $2,038.80 to $0.00, Computers; $2,250.00 to $439.29, Supplies and Materials; and $4,650.00 to $0.00, Transportation Costs, and establishing Strategic Carryover for Fiscal Year 2023-2024, for a combined total amount of $7,128.09, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
headline: Moves money at McClymonds High from computers, supplies and buses to 2023-24 carryover
summary: On the Measure N Commission's recommendation, McClymonds High School is cutting computers ($2,038.80) and transportation ($4,650.00) to $0 and lowering supplies and materials from $2,250.00 to $439.29. The resolution says the combined amount carried over to fiscal year 2023-24 is $7,128.09. This reallocates money already in the school's 2022-23 plan.
source_issue: The three listed reductions ($2,038.80, $1,810.71 and $4,650.00) total $8,499.51, but the stated combined amount is $7,128.09, which matches counting only $439.29 for supplies and materials.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
